name: Nikolsdorf
kurzbeschreibung: Rural community in the Drautal valley, featuring traditional architecture and untouched landscapes.
beschreibung:
Overview

Nikolsdorf is situated in the Upper Drau Valley at the eastern edge of the sun-drenched Lienz valley basin in the district of Lienz, East Tyrol, approximately twelve kilometers east of the district capital Lienz at an altitude of 637 meters. As the easternmost municipality in the entire federal state of Tyrol, Nikolsdorf directly borders the province of Carinthia at the historic narrow pass known as the Kärntner Tor. The unified community counts roughly 860 residents across 33.6 square kilometers, encompassing the three historic villages of Nikolsdorf, Lengberg, and Nörsach. Nestled on the gentle southern foothills of the Kreuzeck range, the municipality commands majestic views of the jagged limestone spires of the Lienz Dolomites. Nikolsdorf gained international renown through revolutionary textile discoveries at Schloss Lengberg and serves as the home to East Tyrol's sole airfield and a key staging post along the Drau Cycle Path.

History

Settlement of this strategic passage dates to prehistoric antiquity. Lengberg Castle was first documented in 1190; from 1212 until 1803, the lordship of Lengberg formed an enclave of the Archbishopric of Salzburg within Tyrolean lands. In 2008, conservation work at Schloss Lengberg yielded a global archaeological sensation: hidden within a 15th-century vault cavity, researchers discovered over 2,700 textile fragments, including four linen brassieres scientifically radiocarbon-dated to between 1440 and 1485. The finding revised fashion history by disproving the long-held belief that modern brassieres were only invented around 1900. Another cultural jewel is the late Gothic pilgrimage chapel of St. Chrysanthen in Nörsach, consecrated in 1485, celebrated for its winged altarpieces and historic stone offering table. The main village parish church is dedicated to St. Bartholomew.

Getting There

Reaching Nikolsdorf is straightforward and rapid along the primary trans-Alpine Drau Valley corridor. By car, motorists take the B100 Drautalstraße from Lienz traveling twelve minutes eastwards, or arrive from Carinthia via Spittal an der Drau and Oberdrauburg, with the provincial border lying just four kilometers away. Rail passengers utilize the historic Drau Valley Railway, stopping at Nikolsdorf station served regularly by Austrian Federal Railways (ÖBB) S-Bahn line S1, offering spacious carriage capacity for bicycles along the cycle route. For general aviation, the village boasts the public airfield Lienz-Nikolsdorf (ICAO: LOKL), certified for visual flight rules (VFR) catering to private, sport, and charter aircraft.

Tips

A flagship attraction for aviation enthusiasts is the Lienz-Nikolsdorf Airfield, managed by the Lienzer Dolomiten Flying Club. Renowned for its exceptional thermal updrafts, it is celebrated as an international alpine gliding hotspot where visitors can book scenic sightseeing flights soaring over the Großglockner and Lienz Dolomites. Cyclists cherish the award-winning 5-star Drau Cycle Path (R1), winding directly along the riverbanks through the municipal lands. History lovers should marvel at Schloss Lengberg and tour the pilgrimage church of St. Chrysanthen in Nörsach. For mountain hikers, the sunny southern ridges of the Kreuzeck group offer peaceful alpine ascents, including the rewarding trek up Mount Gaugen at 2,195 meters.
